title: How Vaccines Work
text: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to recognize and fight specific pathogens without causing the disease itself. They typically contain a weakened or inactivated form of a pathogen, a piece of it (such as a protein), or genetic instructions (as in mRNA vaccines) to produce that piece. The immune system responds by producing antibodies and memory cells, so it can respond quickly if exposed to the real pathogen later, often preventing or reducing illness severity.
